subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: In the early general elections, what was the official election symbol of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh founded by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee?
options: A) Deepa (Earthen oil lamp)
B) Lotus
C) Bow and Arrow
D) Rising Sun
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh's election symbol was the 'Deepa' (earthen lamp). The BJP later adopted the 'Lotus' upon its founding in 1980.

questions.question: Nagaland was carved out of Assam to become the 16th state of the Indian Union in which year, following an accord with Naga leaders?
questions.explanation: Nagaland was inaugurated as the 16th state of the Indian Union on 1 December 1963 by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.

questions.question: How many Five Year Plans in total were formulated and implemented in India between 1951 and 2017 before the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog?
options: A) 10 Five Year Plans
B) 15 Five Year Plans
C) 12 Five Year Plans
D) 8 Five Year Plans
questions.explanation: India completed twelve Five Year Plans between 1951 and 2017, with the Twelfth Plan (2012-2017) being the final Five Year Plan.

questions.question: What is the official name of the boundary line demarcating the eastern frontier between India and the Tibet region of China?
options: A) Radcliffe Line
B) Durand Line
C) Curzon Line
D) McMahon Line
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line forms the recognized international boundary between India and Tibet in the eastern sector, drawn in 1914.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: From which parliamentary constituency in Uttar Pradesh did Indira Gandhi contest and win the Lok Sabha election in 1971?
options: A) Rae Bareli
B) Amethi
C) Varanasi
D) Allahabad
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi contested from Rae Bareli in 1971, defeating Raj Narain of the Samyukta Socialist Party.

questions.question: Following their victory in March 1977, the newly elected MPs of the Janata Party took a historic solemn pledge of service at Rajghat administered by:
options: A) Morarji Desai and Charan Singh
B) Jayaprakash Narayan and J.B. Kripalani
C) Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani
D) Jagjivan Ram and George Fernandes
questions.explanation: On 24 March 1977, Jayaprakash Narayan and Acharya J.B. Kripalani administered the solemn pledge to Janata MPs at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.

questions.question: Operation Black Thunder II, which successfully cleared militants from the Golden Temple with transparent live media coverage, was conducted in Punjab in:
options: A) June 1984
B) July 1985
C) May 1988
D) January 1992
questions.explanation: Operation Black Thunder II took place from 9 to 18 May 1988 under DGP K.P.S. Gill, forcing militants to surrender without causing damage to the Sanctum Sanctorum.

questions.question: The principal institutional headquarters of the European Union, hosting the European Commission and Council, is situated in:
options: A) Geneva, Switzerland
B) Strasbourg, France
C) Frankfurt, Germany
D) Brussels, Belgium
questions.explanation: Brussels, Belgium, serves as the de facto administrative capital of the European Union, hosting its primary executive and legislative bodies.

questions.question: In 1951, veteran Gandhian leader Acharya J.B. Kripalani broke away from the Indian National Congress to establish which political party?
options: A) Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party (KMPP)
B) Swatantra Party
C) Bharatiya Jana Sangh
D) Socialist Party
questions.explanation: Acharya Kripalani founded the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party (KMPP) in June 1951, which later merged with the Socialist Party in September 1952 to form the PSP.

questions.question: In June 1948, the Constituent Assembly appointed the Linguistic Provinces Commission to examine demands for state reorganisation, headed by Justice:
options: A) Fazal Ali
B) S.K. Dhar
C) H.N. Kunzru
D) K.M. Panikkar
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad appointed the Linguistic Provinces Commission in June 1948 headed by Justice S.K. Dhar, a retired judge of the Allahabad High Court.

questions.question: In July 1968, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi officially celebrated the dramatic success of the Green Revolution by releasing a commemorative postal stamp titled:
options: A) 'Green Revolution'
B) 'Agricultural Resurgence'
C) 'Wheat Revolution'
D) 'Food Self-Reliance'
questions.explanation: In July 1968, Indira Gandhi released the 'Wheat Revolution' stamp to commemorate India's record foodgrain production of over 16 million tonnes of wheat.

questions.question: During the 1956 Suez Crisis, independent India under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru took which strong diplomatic stance in the United Nations?
options: A) Supported the British and French military intervention to reopen the canal
B) Remained completely indifferent and refused to participate in the UN debates
C) Dispatched Indian combat naval flotillas to assist the Israeli army in Sinai
D) Vehemently condemned the joint military invasion of Egypt by Britain, France, and Israel as imperialist aggression
questions.explanation: Nehru strongly opposed Anglo-French colonialism in Egypt, calling it a blatant assault on Egyptian sovereignty and spearheading Afro-Asian solidarity for Nasser.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the 1967 fourth general elections, the Congress party's popular vote share dropped to approximately 40.8%, which resulted in its parliamentary strength falling to:
options: A) 283 seats, a decline of nearly 80 seats compared to 1962
B) 150 seats, losing power to a coalition government immediately
C) 400 seats, achieving the largest landslide in post-independence history
D) 350 seats, matching its previous general election tally exactly
questions.explanation: The Congress dropped from 361 seats in 1962 to 283 seats in 1967, reflecting widespread public discontent with price inflation, food shortages, and economic hardship.

questions.question: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, which introduced Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) and restructured executive-judicial relations, was based on the recommendations of the:
options: A) Shah Commission
B) Swaran Singh Committee
C) Sarkaria Commission
D) Kothari Commission
questions.explanation: The Congress government appointed the Swaran Singh Committee in 1976 to propose constitutional amendments, recommending the inclusion of Fundamental Duties and parliamentary supremacy.

questions.question: To implement the transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab and resolve boundary claims with Haryana under the 1985 Accord, the Union Government appointed the:
options: A) Eradi Tribunal
B) Sarkaria Commission
C) Mathew Commission
D) Fazal Ali Commission
questions.explanation: Justice K.K. Mathew was appointed in 1985 to determine Hindi-speaking areas of Punjab to be transferred to Haryana in lieu of Chandigarh.

questions.question: The January 1988 mass agitation in Meerut by the Bharatiya Kisan Union led by Mahendra Singh Tikait was specifically sparked by farmers' outrage over:
options: A) The compulsory acquisition of farmland to build an international naval airstrip
B) The enactment of mandatory state taxes on religious village marriages
C) The complete prohibition of all tractor sales in western Uttar Pradesh
D) A steep increase in electricity rates for irrigation tube-wells and unremunerative sugarcane prices
questions.explanation: BKU farmers besieged the Meerut commissioner's office in January 1988 demanding the rollback of higher electricity tariffs, higher sugarcane procurement prices, and debt relief.

questions.question: Following the 1996 general elections, Atal Bihari Vajpayee was sworn in as Prime Minister as leader of the single largest party, but his government resigned after just:
options: A) 13 days, after failing to secure a legislative majority on the floor of the Lok Sabha
B) 3 months
C) 1 year
D) 24 hours
questions.explanation: The 13-day Vajpayee government resigned on 28 May 1996 before a floor test because other parties refused to support the BJP, paving the way for the United Front.

questions.question: Launched in February 2019, the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) provides direct income support of how much money per year to eligible landholding farmer families?
options: A) Rs. 12,000 per year
B) Rs. 6,000 per year (in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000)
C) Rs. 2,000 per year
D) Rs. 25,000 per year
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN provides income support of Rs. 6,000 annually to eligible farmer families in three four-monthly instalments of Rs. 2,000 directly transferred into bank accounts.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The North Atlantic Treaty, which created the collective security organization NATO, was officially signed in Washington D.C. on:
options: A) 24 October 1945
C) 4 April 1949
D) 9 November 1989
questions.explanation: NATO was formed on 4 April 1949 with the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty by 12 Western nations pledging collective defense under Article 5.

questions.question: Following the fall of the Berlin Wall, the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) was officially integrated into the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) on:
options: A) 9 November 1989
B) 25 December 1991
C) 1 January 1993
D) 3 October 1990
questions.explanation: German reunification was officially concluded on 3 October 1990, now celebrated as German Unity Day, ending four decades of Cold War division.

questions.question: In a historic address to the US Congress in September 1990, President George H.W. Bush characterized the international response to the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait as inaugurating a:
options: A) 'New World Order' where rule of law, collective security, and peaceful settlement supersede raw aggression
B) 'Fortress America' focused exclusively on unilateral isolationism
C) 'Universal Imperial Compact' dividing the globe into four military zones
D) 'Post-Capitalist Commonwealth' managed by international trade unions
questions.explanation: President George H.W. Bush heralded the 'New World Order' where international law and collective action under US leadership would prevail in the post-Cold War world.

questions.question: On 1 January 1999, the Euro was formally launched as an official accounting currency by how many founding member countries of the European Union?
options: A) 5 member countries
B) 11 member countries
C) 20 member countries
D) All 27 member countries
questions.explanation: On 1 January 1999, 11 EU countries (Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain) adopted the Euro for accounting purposes.

questions.question: The 'Open Door Policy' unveiled by Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978 was designed to:
options: A) Dismantle all state-owned industries and dissolve the People's Liberation Army
B) Convert the People's Republic of China into a multi-party parliamentary democracy
C) Open China's market to foreign direct investment, technology transfers, and international trade while preserving Communist Party rule
D) Ban all private agricultural farming and enforce total state grain requisitioning
questions.explanation: Deng Xiaoping's Open Door policy initiated historic economic reforms, welcoming foreign capital and advanced technology into designated coastal economic zones while maintaining political control.

questions.question: Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 brokered by the World Bank, the waters of which three eastern rivers were allocated exclusively to India for unrestricted use?
options: A) Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab
B) Ganga, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra
C) Kaveri, Krishna, and Godavari
D) Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty gave India unrestricted use of the three Eastern Rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), while the three Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) were allocated largely to Pakistan.

questions.question: The United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF), established in December 1946 to provide relief to children in war-devastated countries, is headquartered in:
options: A) New York City, USA
B) Geneva, Switzerland
C) Paris, France
D) Rome, Italy
questions.explanation: UNICEF was established on 11 December 1946 by the UN General Assembly and is permanently headquartered in New York City.

questions.question: In international security studies, sovereign states enter into formal military alliances primarily because alliances allow them to:
options: A) Eliminate all domestic crime and abolish civilian police departments
B) Combine their military deterrence capabilities and pool defense resources against common perceived adversaries
C) Adopt an identical constitutional legal code across all allied nations
D) Avoid paying any national taxes or maintaining domestic military forces
questions.explanation: Alliances allow states to combine their armed strength to increase collective deterrence and defense capability against common adversaries, as seen in NATO.

questions.question: Adopted in Paris in June 1994 as a direct institutional outcome of the Rio Earth Summit, the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) focuses on:
options: A) The immediate banning of all space satellite launches to preserve the upper atmosphere
B) The mandatory demolition of all urban skyscrapers taller than fifty storeys
C) Mitigating the effects of drought and arresting land degradation in arid, semi-arid, and dry sub-humid areas, particularly in Africa
D) The creation of an international naval fleet to protect polar iceberg melts
questions.explanation: The UNCCD is the sole legally binding international agreement linking environment and development to sustainable land management in dryland ecosystems.

questions.sub_topic: WSF Fifth Meeting in Porto Alegre
questions.question: In January 2005, the fifth assembly of the World Social Forum returned to its birthplace of Porto Alegre, Brazil, where participants adopted the manifesto titled the:
options: A) Washington Consensus Charter
B) Davos Corporate Declaration
C) Bretton Woods Monetary Protocol
D) Porto Alegre Manifesto (Twelve Proposals for Another Possible World)
questions.explanation: At WSF 2005 in Porto Alegre, a group of prominent intellectuals and activists drafted the 'Porto Alegre Manifesto', outlining twelve proposals for debt cancellation, taxing financial transactions, and agrarian reform.

questions.question: In April 1950, Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee resigned from Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's Union Cabinet because of his deep disagreement over the:
options: A) Nehru-Liaquat Pact concerning the protection of religious minorities in East and West Pakistan
B) Adoption of the First Five Year Plan's agricultural targets
C) Creation of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS)
D) Appointment of Sukumar Sen as Chief Election Commissioner
questions.explanation: Dr. Mukherjee resigned as Minister for Industry and Supply in April 1950, protesting that the Delhi Pact (Nehru-Liaquat Pact) failed to protect Hindu minorities facing persecution in East Pakistan.

questions.question: The foundational resolution creating the National Development Council in August 1952 established that national plans must be reviewed with State Governments to:
options: A) Abolish all independent revenue powers of state legislatures
B) Strengthen and mobilize the effort and resources of the nation in support of the Plan and promote common economic policies
C) Subordinate state high courts to the administrative oversight of the Planning Commission
D) Transfer state agricultural lands directly to central government ownership
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet resolution established the NDC to ensure that state governments participated directly in formulating and executing national development plans.

questions.question: During the one-year term of the November 1947 Standstill Agreement, relations between the Government of India and the Nizam of Hyderabad deteriorated sharply because the Nizam's government:
options: A) Conducted joint naval maneuvers with the British Royal Navy in the Bay of Bengal.
B) Formally merged its administrative departments into the Madras Legislative Assembly.
C) Advanced a secret loan of Rs. 20 crore to Pakistan in government securities, banned Indian currency, and allowed the extremist Razakar militia to unleash communal terror.
D) Surrendered all state weaponry unconditionally to the Indian Ministry of States.
questions.explanation: The Nizam violated the Standstill Agreement by loaning securities to Pakistan, prohibiting Indian currency, appointing a diplomatic agent to Pakistan, and allowing Kasim Razvi's Razakars to terrorize civilians and attack trains.

questions.question: In September 1952, the Praja Socialist Party (PSP) was formed through the merger of which two prominent opposition political formations that had contested the first general elections?
options: A) The Bharatiya Jana Sangh and the Hindu Mahasabha
B) The Communist Party of India and the Revolutionary Socialist Party
C) The Swatantra Party and the Forward Bloc
D) The Socialist Party (led by Jayaprakash Narayan and Ram Manohar Lohia) and the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party (led by Acharya J.B. Kripalani)
questions.explanation: Following the 1952 elections, the Socialist Party merged with Kripalani's KMPP to form the Praja Socialist Party (PSP), creating a formidable non-communist democratic socialist front.

questions.question: Professor P.C. Mahalanobis's Four-Sector Operational Model developed for the Second Five Year Plan categorized the economy into Sector K (capital goods) and three consumer sectors (C1, C2, and C3). What was the specific role assigned to Sector C2 (household, artisanal, and cottage industries)?
options: A) To generate immediate mass employment and produce consumer goods with low capital investment while heavy investments were locked into Sector K.
B) To manufacture long-range ballistic missiles and heavy combat locomotives exclusively.
C) To absorb 100% of foreign industrial machinery imports from the United States.
D) To export all traditional handicrafts exclusively to the Soviet Union.
questions.explanation: Sector C2 (cottage and small industries) was designed to maximize employment and supply consumer goods using labor-intensive methods, preventing inflation while capital-intensive heavy industries (Sector K) were under construction.

questions.sub_topic: 1959 Border Clashes and Zhou Enlai Proposals
questions.question: In the late 1950s, armed clashes at Longju in the eastern sector (August 1959) and the Kongka Pass in Ladakh (October 1959) led Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai to propose that:
options: A) India should surrender all northeastern hill tracts and dissolve the Indian Army.
B) Both sides withdraw their military forces 20 kilometers from the McMahon Line in the east and from the line of actual control in the west.
C) China should evacuate all military forces from Tibet and restore the Dalai Lama.
D) Both countries should submit the border dispute to binding arbitration by the United States.
questions.explanation: Zhou Enlai proposed a mutual 20-km military disengagement, which Nehru rejected because it would have legitimized China's incursions into Aksai Chin and pushed Indian forces far back within their own territory.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: During the 1969 presidential campaign, what was the primary political argument used by Indira Gandhi's senior cabinet colleagues Jagjivan Ram and Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to justify their call for a 'conscience vote' against their own party's official candidate?
options: A) They argued that the Election Commission of India had officially cancelled the nomination of Sanjiva Reddy.
B) They claimed that V.V. Giri was the official consensus candidate of the United Nations Security Council.

C) They accused Congress President Nijalingappa of entering into an unprincipled, reactionary alliance with right-wing opposition parties (Jana Sangh and Swatantra) to defeat the socialist policies of the government.
D) They maintained that the Constitution of India prohibited any former Chief Minister from serving as President.
questions.explanation: Jagjivan Ram and Ahmed publicly challenged Nijalingappa over his talks with Jana Sangh and Swatantra leaders, arguing that party discipline could not force Congress MPs to vote for a candidate backed by communal and conservative opponents.

questions.question: In the landmark constitutional case Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975), the Supreme Court struck down Article 329A(4) (inserted by the 39th Amendment) on the ground that:
options: A) The 39th Amendment had been passed without a two-thirds majority in the Rajya Sabha.
B) Parliament had no constitutional authority to amend any provision of the Representation of the People Act.
C) The Election Commission of India had not given prior executive permission to amend the Constitution.
D) It abrogated the principle of free and fair elections, equality before the law, and judicial review, which constitute the inviolable Basic Structure of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: A Constitution Bench held that wiping out an election dispute through legislative decree violated the separation of powers, judicial review, and the rule of law, applying the Kesavananda Bharati Basic Structure doctrine for the first time to strike down an amendment.

questions.question: Why was the Mathew Commission unable to finalize the transfer of the city of Chandigarh to Punjab on the scheduled deadline of 26 January 1986 under the Punjab Accord?
options: A) It identified 107 Hindi-speaking villages in Punjab's Fazilka and Abohar tehsils for transfer to Haryana, but could not transfer them because the Punjabi-speaking village of Kandukhera broke territorial contiguity with Haryana.
B) The Supreme Court of India issued an injunction declaring the Punjab Accord unconstitutional.
C) The Chief Minister of Punjab resigned and declared an armed rebellion against the Union.
D) The Government of Haryana officially rejected the possession of Chandigarh.
questions.explanation: Under the principle of contiguity, Fazilka/Abohar could not be transferred without Kandukhera, which voted in a census commission to remain Punjabi-speaking, deadlocking the transfer of Chandigarh.

questions.question: In Maharashtra, the Dalit Panthers and associated Dalit progressive movements waged a protracted social struggle in the late 1970s and 1980s known as the 'Namantar Andolan' demanding:
options: A) The conversion of Mumbai into an autonomous tribal union territory
B) The renaming of Marathwada University in Aurangabad after Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar
C) The abolition of all private Marathi language printing presses
D) The reservation of 100% of all state legislative seats for Dalit writers
questions.explanation: The Namantar Andolan (Name Change Movement) was a 16-year mass struggle to rename Marathwada University after Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, facing violent upper-caste backlash until the compromise name 'Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University' was adopted in 1994.

questions.question: In addition to reservation of seats in public employment and educational institutions, the Mandal Commission report placed vital emphasis on which structural socio-economic reform to uplift backward classes?
options: A) The compulsory nationalization of all urban private residential housing complexes.
B) The abolition of the Indian Administrative Service and replacement by regional militias.
C) Radical agrarian land reforms and redistribution of surplus agricultural land to break the feudal monopoly of landed elites in rural society.
D) The closure of all private commercial trading companies operating in port cities.
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission cautioned that reservations alone could not resolve backwardness without agrarian reform, stating: 'In a society where caste determines status and wealth, the real power lies in land ownership... radical land reforms are essential'.

questions.question: Political scientists characterize the political era following the BJP's consecutive single-party majorities in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections as the emergence of:
options: A) A classical two-party bipartisan duopoly modeled on the United States presidential system
B) A fragmented regional confederation where national parties have ceased to exist
C) An authoritarian single-party state where all opposition parties are legally prohibited
D) The 'Second Dominant Party System' (or BJP-dominant system), replacing the multi-party coalition era of 1989-2014
questions.explanation: Scholars such as Suhas Palshikar argue that the BJP has become the central pole around which national politics revolves (winning 282 seats in 2014 and 303 in 2019), inaugurating India's second dominant party system.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: On the climactic night of 27 October 1962 during the Cuban Missile Crisis, what crucial secret diplomatic arrangement was concluded between Robert Kennedy and Soviet Ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin?
options: A) The US pledged not to invade Cuba and gave a secret unwritten promise to withdraw American Jupiter missiles from Turkey within a few months, in exchange for Soviet missile removal from Cuba.
B) The Soviet Union agreed to surrender all control over East Berlin in exchange for Cuba joining the United Nations.
C) The United States agreed to cede the naval base at Guantanamo Bay to the Soviet Navy.
D) Both superpowers agreed to merge their strategic missile command centers in Vienna.
questions.explanation: Robert Kennedy met Dobrynin to finalize the compromise: Khrushchev would withdraw missiles from Cuba under UN verification, and Kennedy would publicly pledge non-invasion while secretly removing Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

questions.question: The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 gave rise to several protracted, unresolved territorial disputes known as 'frozen conflicts'. Which of the following correctly pairs these breakaway regions with their recognized sovereign states?
options: A) Transnistria — Belarus; Abkhazia — Armenia; Nagorno-Karabakh — Kazakhstan
B) Transnistria — Moldova; Abkhazia and South Ossetia — Georgia; Nagorno-Karabakh — Azerbaijan
C) Transnistria — Ukraine; South Ossetia — Russia; Nagorno-Karabakh — Turkmenistan
D) Transnistria — Romania; Abkhazia — Turkey; Nagorno-Karabakh — Iran
questions.explanation: Ethnic and separatist wars in the early 1990s left de facto pro-Russian breakaway enclaves unrecognized internationally: Transnistria in Moldova, Abkhazia/South Ossetia in Georgia, and Armenian-majority Nagorno-Karabakh in Azerbaijan.

questions.sub_topic: Global Commons of Cyberspace and GPS
questions.question: An example of structural power in US global hegemony is its historical stewardship over global digital commons, exemplified by the fact that:
options: A) Every computer terminal worldwide must obtain an annual operating license from the US Congress.
B) The US government owns 100% of all physical transoceanic undersea fiber optic cables.

C) The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) operated under contract with the US Department of Commerce until 2016, and the Global Positioning System (GPS) is maintained by the US Department of Defense.
D) All foreign internet websites must be written exclusively in the English language.
questions.explanation: US structural hegemony is embedded in digital infrastructure: the internet was created by the Pentagon (ARPANET), domain names were overseen by the US Commerce Department, and GPS is a US military asset provided as a global public good.

questions.question: In the wake of the devastating 1997-98 Asian Financial Crisis and dissatisfaction with IMF conditionalities, the ASEAN+3 countries (ASEAN, China, Japan, and South Korea) established which regional financial safety net in May 2000?
options: A) Asian Monetary Fund under the World Bank
B) Pacific Currency Union pegged to the Euro
C) Bangkok Gold Reserve Syndicate
D) Chiang Mai Initiative (a multilateral currency swap arrangement)
questions.explanation: The Chiang Mai Initiative (CMI) was launched in May 2000 in Thailand by ASEAN+3 finance ministers to establish bilateral currency swap lines, protecting regional economies from speculative currency attacks.

questions.question: Under the maritime boundary agreements signed between India and Sri Lanka in 1974 and 1976 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Prime Minister Sirimavo Bandaranaike:
options: A) India recognized Sri Lankan sovereignty over the uninhabited islet of Katchatheevu in the Palk Strait, while securing access for Indian fishermen to dry nets and visit the St. Anthony church shrine.
B) India annexed the Jaffna peninsula as a special coastal union territory.
C) Sri Lanka ceded all territorial waters in the Gulf of Mannar unconditionally to India.
D) Katchatheevu was placed under direct administrative control of the United Nations Environment Programme.
questions.explanation: The 1974 agreement settled the maritime boundary, ceding Katchatheevu to Sri Lanka, while Article 5 guaranteed traditional access for Indian fishermen to dry nets and attend the annual festival.

questions.question: Launched by UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan in July 2000, the United Nations Global Compact is an international initiative designed to:
options: A) Impose compulsory international tax levies on all commercial airline tickets to finance UN peacekeepers.
B) Encourage multinational corporations and businesses worldwide to adopt sustainable and socially responsible policies in human rights, labor, environment, and anti-corruption.
C) Enforce a mandatory global minimum wage on all agricultural farm workers.
D) Nationalize all private pharmaceutical companies researching viral vaccines.
questions.explanation: The UN Global Compact is a voluntary corporate sustainability initiative based on CEO commitments to align strategies with ten principles in human rights, labor, environment, and anti-corruption.

questions.question: In academic and policy debates on non-traditional security, the 'Narrow' school of Human Security differs from the 'Broad' school because the Narrow school:
options: A) Focuses exclusively on naval submarine warfare, excluding infantry combat.
B) Applies only to citizens residing in small island developing states.

C) Restricts its focus to protection from political violence, state repression, war crimes, and armed conflict ('freedom from fear'), whereas the Broad school includes poverty, hunger, disease, and natural disasters ('freedom from want').
D) Rejects all forms of international law in favor of raw nuclear deterrence.
questions.explanation: Canada and Norway championed the 'narrow' freedom from fear approach (focusing on violence, landmines, ICC), while Japan and UNDP championed the 'broad' freedom from want approach (poverty, disease, environmental hazards).

questions.question: Under Article 2 of the 2015 Paris Climate Agreement, signatory nations legally committed to holding the increase in the global average temperature to:
options: A) Exactly 5°C above pre-industrial levels by the year 2050
B) Below freezing temperature at all polar latitudes year-round
C) Zero degrees Celsius variation compared to the year 2000
D) Well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels
questions.explanation: Article 2(1)(a) of the Paris Agreement sets the global mitigation goal: holding temperature increase to well below 2°C and pursuing efforts to cap it at 1.5°C through Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

questions.question: In his influential 1990 essay 'Disjuncture and Difference in the Global Cultural Economy', anthropologist Arjun Appadurai proposed five conceptual dimensions to understand global cultural flows. These five dimensions are:
options: A) Geoscapes, Chronoscapes, Biomanufactures, Terrascapes, and Astroscapes
B) Ethnoscapes, Technoscapes, Financescapes, Mediascapes, and Ideoscapes
C) Urbanscapes, Ruralscapes, Maritimescapes, Desertscapes, and Polarscapes
D) Linguascapes, Religioscapes, Monetarscapes, Militarscapes, and Jurisscapes
questions.explanation: Appadurai's five 'scapes' describe fluid global flows: Ethnoscapes (moving people), Technoscapes (technology), Financescapes (capital), Mediascapes (information/images), and Ideoscapes (political ideologies/freedom).

questions.question: Following the ratification of the cession of French establishments in India in 1962, Parliament enacted the 14th Constitutional Amendment Act, which created the Union Territory of Pondicherry and inserted which landmark constitutional article?
options: A) Article 370, granting autonomous treaty-making powers to French citizens
B) Article 356, permitting the dismissal of the President of India
C) Article 239A, empowering Parliament to create local legislatures and councils of ministers for certain Union Territories
D) Article 368, abolishing judicial review over all foreign boundary agreements
questions.explanation: The 14th Amendment incorporated Pondicherry into the First Schedule and inserted Article 239A, authorizing Parliament to establish elected legislatures and cabinets for Union Territories (Puducherry, and later others).
